acp.description: ACP protocol semantics: binding and override, spawn/cancel, parent/child message relay and delivery (event streams, completion notify), message blocks, and ACP client/server compatibility — not necessarily ACPX-specific. The session objects themselves belong to `sessions`.

acpx.description: ACPX protocol, transport, proxy, worker/backend process, configured binding, compatibility, and files or commands explicitly named ACPX.

agent_runtime.description: OpenClaw's internal agent machinery: runtime startup, loop, backends, model call orchestration, runtime adapter behavior, subagent execution and orchestration, and runtime ownership/execution architecture. External coding-agent integrations belong to `coding_agent_integrations`; ACP protocol/session/delivery work belongs to `acp`/`acpx`.

api_surface.description: External API, CLI, HTTP, and SDK contracts: REST endpoints, webhooks, SSE, OpenResponses, chat completions, documented command contracts, and request/response shapes.

approvals.description: Approval flows, permission decisions, approval prompts, approve/deny commands, approval mode behavior, policy checks, and pending approval state.

auth_identity.description: OpenClaw's own authentication and identity surface: login, auth profiles, OAuth flows, tokens, account binding, credential propagation, device identity, and credential scope within the product. Not for authentication of external services touched incidentally.

browser_automation.description: Browser automation, CDP/Chrome integration, browser session attach, auth browser flows, screenshots, browser vision, and web interaction tooling.

chat_integrations.description: Chat platform integrations, channel adapters, message ingestion, and delivery surfaces such as Discord, Telegram, Slack, Feishu, WhatsApp, Zulip, Mattermost, and webchat.

codex.description: Items that explicitly involve the Codex runtime, Codex auth, Codex ACP, Codex plugin, or Codex command compatibility.

coding_agent_integrations.description: OpenClaw's integration with external coding-agent runtimes or CLIs such as Pi, Codex, Claude Code, Gemini CLI, or similar: launching them, configuring them, authenticating them, adapting their protocol, routing work to them, handling compatibility, or preserving their runtime contract. Internal OpenClaw orchestration does not qualify unless OpenClaw's behavior toward an external coding-agent runtime changes.

config.description: Configuration as a surface: schemas, persisted config shape, config loading/validation/repair, defaults, environment variables, allow/deny configuration, policy settings, and adding or changing user- or operator-facing settings (toggles, pickers, defaults, persisted preferences), including when surfaced through a settings UI.

cron_automation.description: Cron jobs, scheduled runs, heartbeat automation, one-shot jobs, force-run behavior, and recurring task execution.

docs.description: Documentation, guides, README changes, spelling, taxonomy, and explanatory content — when the documentation itself is the subject.

exec_tools.description: Shell execution, command invocation, PATH handling, exec tools, command allowlists, tool execution policy, execution output control, and durable process handling.

gateway.description: OpenClaw gateway behavior when the gateway itself is the owning surface: daemon startup/restart, HTTP gateway routes, gateway protocol/state, gateway-owned execution, service health, and gateway-managed lifecycle.

hooks.description: Hook registration, hook lifecycle, hook events, hook priority, hook payloads, hook filtering, hook security, and managed hook behavior.

inference_api.description: The integration layer between OpenClaw and model serving/providers: usage of Responses, Chat Completions, Anthropic Messages, and similar inference APIs; streaming/SSE and usage chunks; base URL normalization; request/response handling for inference, including TTS, vision, and embeddings API integrations; and adding or configuring inference providers (setup, auth, routing, catalogs, compatibility).

mcp_tooling.description: MCP server or client behavior, MCP allow/deny rules, conformance checks, handshake/tool behavior, MCP config, tool discovery and materialization (tools/list and resources), and tool invocation compatibility.

memory.description: Memory systems, memory indexing/search, embeddings, vector stores, active memory, LanceDB, memory provider state, and memory archival or recovery.

model_lifecycle.description: Introduction, decommissioning, or adjustment of model configurations: adding/removing/renaming model IDs, catalog and default updates, deprecations, version-specific model support, and model metadata (context windows, quantization variants) changes.

notifications.description: Generic notification policy and outbound delivery behavior: completion delivery paths, delivery gates, notify settings, announcements, and sent-message handling. Emitting events or hooks about sends belongs to `hooks` unless the outbound delivery path/gate itself is implemented or changed.

packaging_deployment.description: Build, packaging, installers, Docker images, release artifacts, deployment, service managers, SEA, launchd, systemd, pnpm, and runtime distribution.

queueing.description: Queues, lanes, task state, follow-up queues, scheduling, run ordering, work dispatch, locks gating dispatch, stuck jobs, and backpressure.

reliability.description: Reliability behavior: timeouts, crashes, leaks, stuck state, retries, data loss, lifecycle cleanup, recovery, overload, races, and operational failure modes.

sandboxing.description: Sandbox policy, sandbox inheritance, sandbox escape, path isolation, containers, Docker, process limits, filesystem hiding, and execution boundaries.

security.description: Concrete security issues, improvements, and direct security features: SSRF, private-network access, credential/secret/token exposure or hardening, auth or permission boundaries, access-control enforcement, HMAC/signature verification, sandbox escape, vulnerabilities, and supply-chain hardening. Not for privacy-focused product features unless they change a security control.

self_hosted_inference.description: Integration with inference engines and local model operation such as vLLM, llama.cpp, Ollama, LM Studio, TGI, LocalAI, GGUF/quantization, local hardware/VRAM behavior, local model fallback/context behavior, or self-hosted embeddings/speech/memory backends — whether on device or self-hosted elsewhere.

sessions.description: The session objects themselves: session identity, lifecycle, state, persistence, transcript, resume, reset, cleanup, parent/child session lifecycle and state, and session stores. ACP parent/child message semantics and delivery belong to `acp`; internal spawning or relay mechanisms do not imply `sessions` unless stored session records or lifecycle/state change.

skills_plugins.description: Skills/plugins as product surfaces: SKILL.md, managed skills, plugin manifests/loading/registration, plugin SDK/runtime APIs, MCP Apps, plugin hooks, SecretRefs, skill sync/prelude/wrappers, and doctor/check behavior for plugin or skill surfaces (the bundled Policy plugin is a plugin surface).

telemetry_usage.description: OpenClaw's own telemetry and usage surface: token/usage/cost accounting, metrics, diagnostics, trace production and observability coverage, and status reporting of the product. Not for measurement or benchmark vocabulary adjacent to another surface's change.

tests_ci.description: Tests, CI, fixtures, coverage, mocks, and platform-specific test fixes — when test infrastructure itself is the subject.

tool_calling.description: Model tool-calling behavior: tool-call protocol, tool-call deltas, function/tool schemas, tool result transcript handling, tool result routing, and tool-call rendering.

ui_tui.description: User interface behavior as the changed or failing surface: UI/TUI display, interaction, navigation, rendering, dashboards, status views, footer, mobile UI, and settings screens. Not for defects merely observed through a UI when the failing behavior belongs to another surface.
